decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach toward the two nearer white supports; pitch grippers down gradually, keeping each arm in its own workspace.
Align open grippers to the near supports' visible long axes and descend gradually; grasp centering remains uncertain until wrist views.
Refine centering, close both grippers fully, and test retention with a short vertical lift.
Both supports appear retained. Carry them inward above their base positions and straighten their long axes before lowering.
Lower the two upright supports to the tabletop at symmetric base positions, then open without lateral motion.
Withdraw vertically from the released supports, then move outward while turning toward the two ends of the long lower board.
Align both grippers across the long board's ends while descending above it; the two released supports appear upright and symmetric.
Descend to the board grasp height at both ends, then close fully while holding the board level.
Lift the long board evenly with both grippers closed, then carry it toward the upright supports with clearance.
Center the retained board over the two supports, lower it level to the lower-layer height, and release without lateral motion.
The lower board appears stable on both upright supports. Withdraw upward, then move toward the remaining outer white blocks for the middle layer.
Approach the remaining white blocks from above, matching their visible slanted long axes. Keep grippers open for wrist-view alignment.
Refine wrist-view yaw alignment and lower to the white-block grasp height, keeping both grippers open until centering is visible.
Make small centering corrections, close fully around both white blocks, and lift vertically to check retention before transport.
Both blocks appear retained. Carry them inward above the lower board and straighten their axes, retaining vertical clearance.
Place the two middle supports symmetrically on the lower board, lowering vertically before releasing. Verify stability after withdrawal.
Withdraw above the released middle supports, then approach the shorter board's ends from the front without disturbing the lower layer.
The middle supports remain upright. Finish aligning both grippers with the shorter board and descend together just above its grasp height.
Lower to the shorter board, close both grippers fully, and make a small level lift to verify retention.
The shorter board appears retained at both ends. Lift above the middle supports and carry it rearward while keeping it level.
Center the level shorter board above the middle supports, then lower vertically to contact while retaining both grasps.
Settle the middle board on both supports, open both grippers, then withdraw outward and upward to check the completed layer.
The middle layer appears stable. Move the left arm above the small brown top board while parking the right arm clear of the tower.
Refine alignment with the small board's long axis and descend with the left gripper open; the right arm stays clear.
Lower to the thin board, make a small yaw correction, close the left gripper fully, and test the grasp with a vertical lift.
The small board appears retained. Lift above the tower and carry inward while turning its long axis across the middle board.
Carry the retained small board over the tower center and finish straightening it, maintaining clearance above the middle layer.
Lower the centered small board slowly toward the middle layer, retaining the grasp until contact height is clearer.
Set the small board down with a short final descent, open the left gripper, and withdraw diagonally away from the tower to inspect stability.
The small top board appears stable. Retract the left arm toward its home side while bringing the right gripper above the green top piece.
Lower and center the right gripper on the green piece, close fully, and test a short lift. Continue the left arm's gradual return clear of the tower.
The green piece appears retained. Lift it above the tower before moving inward, while finishing the left arm's return to origin.
Carry the retained green piece level above the small top board, keeping clearance and the left arm at origin.
Refine the green piece's horizontal centering over the small board and lower slowly while retaining the grasp.
Settle the green piece gently onto the small board, open the right gripper, and withdraw upward and outward to check tower stability.
The tower is upright, but the green piece appears left of the small board's center. Regrasp and lift it slightly for a small centering correction.
Shift the retained green piece about two centimeters right to center it on the small board, lower vertically, and release.
The green piece now appears centered. Withdraw the open right gripper clear of the tower and begin a gradual elbow-up return to origin.
All eight pieces appear upright and centered. Continue returning the open right arm toward origin, maintaining clearance and configuration continuity.
Finish the right arm's return to origin with decreasing increments; keep both grippers open and leave the upright tower untouched.
